## 🎓 Today's lesson
- **What is an S-1 IPO Filing?**
  When a private company wants to list its shares on a US stock exchange, it must submit a detailed registration form called Form S-1 to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). This public document acts as a comprehensive handbook for investors, revealing audited financial statements, actual compute expenses, management compensation, ownership stakes, and key risk factors. For example, Anthropic's new S-1 filing put its huge compute costs in focus, giving Wall Street real data to evaluate AI business models [[The New York Times]](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxNQ0gwS2ZOLWduOWZzM1FvdFNodDZnTU91SWR0U1dCY2VxOGxQcXY0THNnanJjWFhYb054WXotQWlvNTYwa2g3aTVEXzllX1pfTHcyTGhZVG1NT25MSmwzd0xUQ1c3VGdJbGJ1OHZPSm53d05zc3g2cGV2X3JlaTRGY3c3U045cUdO?oc=5) [[CNBC]](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMingFBVV95cUxNYUVHWGxUWVFOQnhHOEpjMEx2V0lHWG1PTnlJV0lNOUlWZXlfa1RYZHQwYWt1TGRSMFdyNnIzN3VfelAxemhFTDFoX241eEpMMDhTSWRwS0pGX3Vtanl1TUJJemI0Y0JVc21mRXg4Z2NDSmwyaS1kQWk1SG56VUNCLTJTcnRQQkh2a0d5YmgwSmhFTVRtVlZrM3pkdGREdw?oc=5).
